-73.19410,44.47970.name: University of Vermont Medical Center, Vermont Center for Reproductive Medicine
-73.19410,44.47970.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Elizabeth McGee, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-118.53378,34.17012.name: Institute For Obstetrics Gynecology & Infertility
-118.53378,34.17012.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

10.00132,53.55017.name: Evotec SE
10.00132,53.55017.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-76.94181,39.00428.name: Department of Veterinary Medicine
-76.94181,39.00428.state: 8075 Greenmead Drive College Park, MD 20742, United States
-76.94181,39.00428.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by University of Maryland. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-77.45400,38.80600.name: ATCC
-77.45400,38.80600.desc: The American Type Culture Collection holds and distributes cell lines, microbes and viruses — the standard reference material biology is calibrated against. Its catalogue is the reason results from two laboratories can be compared at all. Access requires institutional credentials, so like Addgene it is simultaneously the infrastructure of open science and a gate that decides who may practise it. It is a reference collection rather than a distribution repository: strains are held so that work done in any laboratory can be compared against the same authenticated organism, which is a different job from a repository built to circulate engineered constructs.

34.81000,31.89000.name: Evogene
34.81000,31.89000.desc: An Israeli company using computational biology to design traits, licensing them to seed companies rather than selling seed. Like KeyGene, it is a layer beneath the visible market: counting brands in a seed catalogue understates how few sources the underlying genetics has.

126.99000,37.57000.name: CJ CheilJedang — fermentation and feed
126.99000,37.57000.desc: A major producer of fermentation-derived feed additives and food ingredients, competing directly with Ajinomoto. Two or three companies supply most of the world’s fermented amino acids, which is a concentration comparable to seed and attracts none of the same attention because the product is an ingredient nobody sees.

101.69600,2.92700.name: JAKIM — Malaysian halal certification
101.69600,2.92700.desc: Certifies halal status for food sold to around two billion people, and its rulings cover enzymes, gelatine and cultured products made with engineered organisms. Whether a protein made by a modified microbe carries the origin of the gene it came from is a question no food regulator answers and this one must.

-71.08500,42.36000.name: Gradient — litigation science consulting
-71.08500,42.36000.desc: Produces exposure and risk assessments used by manufacturers in litigation and in regulatory comment. Consulting science of this kind is published in peer-reviewed journals and cited like any other work, and the funding relationship is disclosed in a line most readers do not reach.
